lines.x: 'Assistant'? Just tell me what to do. Doesn't matter if I know how. I can learn, as long as you can teach me.

My birthplace and background? Didn't I have those on my resumé? I don't mind you asking, there's just nothing worth mentioning. Sorry, I'm no good at small talk. Mm, maybe you're right. Maybe I'll get better at it one day, but right now, I just work harder when I get time to chat.

Something off about this piece of paper? You're right. Someone stuck this odd scrap sheet to my door, and I don't want it going to waste, so I'm practicing my writing on it—Oh, it's an invitation to a party? *sigh* I couldn't read it back then. Besides, the date here was last week.

Zelgrad… I was born on its foundations. After I grew up, I took up Mama and Papa's gear, and kept building the city. We built the dormitory ten stories high, but it still couldn't compare to that stone wall. Lies, cover-ups, I don't give a crap, but why'd they have to destroy our home?

The thing I picked up off the ground? Nothing, just an empty pill bottle. What do you mean, 'it's dirty'? Medicine kills disease. Once I wash it, Grisha and Masha will have the building blocks they always wanted. I collected a lot of bottles like this one…

Lyudmila and I? No, you got it wrong. Calling ourselves 'Reunion' wasn't her idea. Back then, most people in the city didn't really know what Reunion stood for or what they did, but a name that brings change is enough to make it happen when you're talking life or death.

I got something to report. I've been helping out at Engineering lately, and uh… got paid today. I don't know if Rhodes Island's rules allow that—Really? I'll eat it without worry then. Hmm? No, of course it's not money. It's some vegetable stew that Alanna lady gave me.

Sorry to bother you, but how do you say these words? 'Agony', 'oath', 'adore', and 'remorse'. Oh, I see. Thanks. What book am I reading? I just grabbed a random one from the library. I heard it's a popular new romance novel, but I don't get the people in the story, so I can't really say if I like it.

As I walked in, I suddenly realized I've been talking a lot more since I came here. Words are like water pouring from a kettle. The more you say, the lighter your heart gets. This feeling of lightness makes me anxious, so I'll be going as soon as my shift is over. But I'm coming on time tomorrow, Doctor.
Napping during work hours, not scared of what the boss might say… Wait, I think that is the boss.
Hello, I'm Tonya. Lyudmila said I could find work here, and get the kids treated at the same time—Yes, they're my little brother and sister. Come, say hello to the Doctor.
Do I have to do things this way? Just checking. I can do them, don't matter if they're good or bad.

Let go, Grisha, it's not a toy. Masha, please, give me that ribbon. Okay, you can wear the medal to bed, as long as the Doctor says it's okay—Sorry, Doctor. They really wanted to see the promotion ceremony.
What good does this medal do? No, I'm not talking about my salary or my prescription. I mean, once I accept it, will I be able to do more, save more people?
As you say.
I'll do my best.
Steady hands, quick feet, clear head.
Deep breaths. Hands, no shaking. Double-check before hitting.
Me?
Mm. I'm ready.
I go anywhere.
You're the boss.
Little kids hit harder than this.
A scratch like this is nothing.
'Stop resisting'? Do you think we're idiots?
'Drop your weapons'? Why not just kill ourselves?
Still stressed about what happened, or glad it's over? Haha… I don't know why I'm laughing either.
No matter how glorious sacrifice is, I hope we need less of it in the future. You protected us. You did very good.
I want to save just one more soul. If we get another shot or not, this is your call. And I'm waiting on it.
Can I live with that…? Of course not.
Big bed, but I have to stay in the ward with the kids every night, so I can't sleep in it. Shame.
You scared me. Incredible.
You like watching people work? I don't mind, it will not bother me. Be even better if you want to help out.
Arknights.

Strung lights and parties are all new to me. Thanks for bringing me up here so I can see. In a few hours, I have to go make dinner, get the children from class, change my bandages, and clean up the dormitory. I really want to watch this with you a bit longer, Doctor, but…
The more you rush, the more you have to take it slow. As long as you don't stop, you'll always get the job done.

I used the cafeteria oven to bake you a cake—Wait. Before you dig in, try a bite first. I'm not very good at baking. I used to sprinkle a little sugar on some sliced bread for my brother and sister's birthdays, but now I don't have to worry about rationing, I'm worried I might have gotten greedy with the sweetness.

Grisha and Masha been doing good in their reading classes, the little one got out of Intensive Care, and Logistics helped me find some simple part-time work—Why am I telling you this? Err… When I first came to Rhodes Island, I thought it was just a temporary job, but now, I want to stay here.
